## What I make of it (the honest synthesis)

- **The raw association is real but mostly main-effects.** Source main effects alone reach pooled LOFO ρ 0.776; the target-permutation null (which preserves them) puts the band at 0.591; the within-source z-normed read is 0.235. So S's pair-level increment over "which source was trained" is modest — real (null cleared at p = 0.0079; tercile reads 0.18–0.38 within cosine bands), but a minority of the raw 0.613.
- **The redundancy is specifically with the committed #532 cosine.** S survives partialling on JS (0.419), on prompt-surface token-Jaccard (0.589), and on the same-bank same-layer fresh cosine (0.416); it dies only against the committed L21 cosine measured on #532's own bank (0.073). Per plan §4.7 item 5's registered rule, a Confirmed that died against the same-bank cosine would have been "Redressed-in-substance"; the converse situation here — Redressed against the committed covariate while surviving the same-bank read — does NOT upgrade the verdict (the lattice keys on the committed covariate alone), but it does mean "function space added nothing beyond representation distance" is only demonstrated against the incumbent's exact operationalization.
- **Absolute transfer is poor; the signal is the ranking.** S_sym is negative for most pairs (quantiles p0 −9.82, p25 −2.77, median +0.18, max 0.61): a family's map usually predicts another family's answers WORSE than that family's mean answer. Cross-context "interchangeable computation" in the literal R² sense does not hold; what predicts leakage is the relative ordering of how badly maps transfer.
- **Symmetrization caps the achievable ρ.** By the registered formula, var(L−Lᵀ)/2 ÷ var(L) = 0.740 on the 16×16 subgrid (1.0 = iid-noise-level asymmetry): most of L's variance there is direction-asymmetric, which no symmetric predictor can carry; the 0.988 attenuation ceiling does not account for this. Consistent with that, the directional read ρ(S_trans(i→j), L) = 0.670 exceeds the symmetric 0.613 (descriptive; committed in `analyzer_free_reads.json`, registered inference not run).
- **H2's substance fails cleanly.** Adding S to any stack — or adding ANY pair feature to plain additive effects — hurts held-out-target CV-R². The pair-level structure the features carry does not extrapolate to unseen target families under OLS.

- **The raw association is real but mostly main-effects.** Source main effects alone reach pooled LOFO ρ 0.776; the target-permutation null (which preserves them) puts the band at 0.591 — ~4× the plan's registered expectation of ≈0.1–0.15, a plan-time miss worth naming — and the within-source z-normed read is 0.235. - **The redundancy is specifically with the committed #532 cosine — and the kill covariate has a bank-specific advantage.** S survives partialling on JS (0.419 [0.067, 0.707]), on prompt-surface token-Jaccard (0.589), and on the same-bank same-layer fresh cosine (0.416 [0.103, 0.667] — CI-grade as of this revision); it dies only against the committed L21 cosine measured on #532's own bank (0.073). Raw strength points the same way: the committed cosine out-correlates S (0.622 vs 0.613) while the SAME cosine recipe at the SAME L21 recomputed on OUR fresh bank reads only 0.389 — the committed matrix shares measurement provenance (the #532 probe bank) with the DV, a concrete alternative explanation for why the kill fires only against the incumbent's exact operationalization. Per plan §4.7 item 5's registered rule the lattice keys on the committed covariate, so the verdict stays Redressed — but "function space added nothing beyond representation distance" is demonstrated only against that covariate.
- **Absolute transfer is poor; the signal is the ranking.** S_sym is negative for 43% of the 400 pairs (directional S_trans: 46%); quantiles p0 −9.82, p25 −2.77, median +0.18, max 0.61. So a large minority of cross-family map transfers predict another family's answers worse than that family's mean answer, and even the best sits far below the same-family split-half benchmark (mean own-map transfer R² = 0.496). Cross-context "interchangeable computation" in the literal R² sense does not hold; what predicts leakage is the relative ordering of how well (or badly) maps transfer.
- **Symmetrization caps the achievable ρ.** The registered statistic var(L−Lᵀ)/2 ÷ var(L) is calibrated so 1.0 = iid-noise-level asymmetry (it is 2× the raw asymmetric-variance fraction). On the 16×16 subgrid it reads 0.740 with the 16 diagonal self-cells included (the committed number) and 0.945 on the off-diagonal mask the analysis uses everywhere else — i.e. roughly **37–47% of L's variance there is direction-asymmetric** (74–94% of the iid-noise level), which no symmetric predictor can carry. The implied Pearson ceiling for any symmetric predictor is ≈ 0.73–0.79, so the observed 0.613 sits near it; the 0.988 attenuation ceiling does not account for this. Consistent with that, the directional read ρ(S_trans(i→j), L) = 0.670 exceeds the symmetric 0.613 (descriptive; committed in `analyzer_free_reads.json`, registered inference not run).
- **H2's substance fails cleanly — and hardest exactly where prediction would matter.** Adding S to any stack — or adding ANY pair feature to plain additive effects — hurts held-out-target CV-R². On the source axis, per-fold skill is near zero for 4 of 5 persona-class sources (see Registered reads 3): the pair-level structure the features carry does not extrapolate to unseen families under OLS, and least of all to unseen personas.

Per plan §4.7 item 5's registered rule the lattice keys on the committed covariate, so the verdict stays Redressed — but "function space added nothing beyond representation distance" is demonstrated only against that covariate.
- **Absolute transfer is poor; the signal is the ranking.** S_sym is negative for 43% of the 400 pairs (directional S_trans: 46%); quantiles p0 −9.82, p25 −2.77, median +0.18, max 0.61. So a large minority of cross-family map transfers predict another family's answers worse than that family's mean answer, and the distribution sits well below the same-family split-half benchmark — median +0.18 vs mean own-map transfer R² 0.496 — though the top of the range is the exception: 76 of the 400 pairs meet or exceed that mean benchmark, and the top 20 (max 0.61) exceed even the best single family's own split-half (0.567). Cross-context "interchangeable computation" in the literal R² sense does not hold for the typical pair; what predicts leakage is the relative ordering of how well (or badly) maps transfer.
- **Symmetrization caps the achievable ρ.** The registered statistic var(L−Lᵀ)/2 ÷ var(L) is calibrated so 1.0 = iid-noise-level asymmetry (it is 2× the raw asymmetric-variance fraction). On the 16×16 subgrid it reads 0.740 with the 16 diagonal self-cells included (the committed number) and 0.945 on the off-diagonal mask the analysis uses everywhere else — i.e. roughly **37–47% of L's variance there is direction-asymmetric** (74–94% of the iid-noise level), which no symmetric predictor can carry. - **H2's substance fails cleanly — and hardest exactly where prediction would matter.** Adding S to any stack — or adding ANY pair feature to plain additive effects — hurts held-out-target CV-R². On the source axis, per-fold skill is near zero for 4 of 5 persona-class sources (see Registered reads 3): the pair-level structure the features carry does not extrapolate to unseen families under OLS, and least of all to unseen personas.
